text: About 3,200 years ago, the Phoenicians lived in port cities where Lebanon is today.
An Egyptian story tells of a man who sailed to Byblos to buy cedar wood.
src: flourished from about 1200 BCE / The Phoenicians were the people of the coastal cities of the northern Levant ... roughly present-day Lebanon
The Egyptian Story of Wenamun ... Its hero, an official of the temple of Amun at Karnak sent to buy cedar ... is kept waiting for weeks in the harbour of Byblos

text: Each of their cities, such as Tyre, Sidon or Byblos, had its own king.
Kings were buried in carved stone coffins, like this one of King Eshmunazar of Sidon.
src: not one nation but rival city-states such as Tyre, Sidon, Byblos and Arwad, each with its own king
kings were laid in stone sarcophagi inscribed with curses on anyone who disturbed them, like Ahiram at Byblos and Tabnit and Eshmunazar II at Sidon

text: Their workshops made glass vessels and beads, jewellery and carved ivory.
Their merchants sold cedar and cloth dyed purple with sea snails across the Near East.
src: Workshops also produced glass vessels and beads, jewellery, seals and amulets / Craftsmen worked ivory, bronze, silver, gold and glass
Their merchants sold cedar, purple cloth, ivory and metalwork across the Near East / Dyers extracted purple from murex sea snails

text: Skilled sailors, they founded towns from Cyprus to Spain, like Tharros in Sardinia.
One of these towns, Carthage in North Africa, grew into a great power.
src: The Phoenicians were the most skilled shipbuilders and navigators of their age / founded settlements from Cyprus to Spain / at Nora, Sulcis and Tharros in Sardinia
Carthage grew into a power in its own right, the centre of the Punic Empire

text: Later the Persians ruled their cities, and King Tennes of Sidon led a revolt.
Then Alexander the Great captured Tyre, and thousands of its people were sold into slavery.
src: In 539 BCE the cities passed under the Achaemenid Empire / Around 351 BCE Sidon, under its king Tennes, led a revolt against the Persian king Artaxerxes III
Alexander the Great takes Tyre after a siege of about seven months / by the ancient accounts between 13,000 and 30,000 of its people were sold into slavery

text: Their greatest gift was the alphabet, carved on this king’s coffin about 3,000 years ago.
It became the ancestor of the Greek, Latin, Hebrew and Arabic scripts.
src: a fixed set of 22 letters, written from right to left, which appears fully formed in the epitaph that Ittobaal, king of Byblos, carved on the sarcophagus of his father Ahiram around 1000 BCE / The Phoenicians’ most lasting creation was their alphabet
is the ancestor of the Greek, Latin, Hebrew and Arabic scripts
